summary.text: A 27-year-old male patient presented with a visual field defect in the right eye that had started 2 days earlier. He had a history of bilateral barrier laser photocoagulation and implantable collamer lens insertion. Best-corrected visual acuity was counting fingers at 50 cm and the anterior segment was unremarkable. The fundus showed macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment from 8 to 1 o’clock with a horseshoe tear at 8.5 o’clock, lattice degeneration with multiple atrophic holes, and previous laser scars.

Scleral encircling was performed on the day of the initial visit, with cryotherapy applied to the tear. One week after surgery the subretinal fluid had significantly decreased, with minimal fluid at the macula and some residual fluid around the tear, and the tear was only partially supported by the encircling band. Three weeks after surgery the subretinal fluid around the tear had increased again.

On the day of the three-week finding, intravitreal 100% perfluoropropane gas (0.35 mL) was injected and the patient was instructed to keep a prone position by day and left side down while sleeping. Four days later (postoperative day 25) the fluid had decreased and barrier laser was applied around the tear. At five weeks temporal fluid increased; a second pure C_(3)F_(8) injection (0.4 mL) was given with strict left side down positioning, and one week later, at 6 weeks, the fluid had resolved and additional laser was applied.

Two months after surgery the retina remained attached with a small macular subretinal fluid bleb not connected to the tear. At 3 months postoperatively there was no detachment and no new breaks; a BCVA of 20 / 30 is reported without a stated time. The authors report recurrent detachment after the first PR and successful reattachment after the second PR with strict positioning; PVR was absent, PR was preferred over revision, and vitrectomy was avoided.
